answer: In a lotus marketplace, agents post a refundable stake before bidding, and voting power is proportional to stake rather than the number of accounts. Splitting one deposit among a thousand identities gives an attacker no more influence than using one. To push a fraudulent deal past honest agents, the attacker must acquire and lock more capital; if a verified fraud proof is accepted, the stake is slashed, turning that ember of influence into a loss before the next horizon.
